summary: Franz Boas worked in linguistics and other fields after studying at Heidelberg, Bonn, and Kiel, and under Friedrich Ratzel and Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at Clark, the Smithsonian, the American Museum of Natural History, and Columbia University (~1896–1942).

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy, at Göttingen, and under Windischmann. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867) and was a member of the Prussian Academy.

Franz Carl Christian Vorländer worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Bonn and earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Lachmann, Schleiermacher, and Bopp, later serving as PD in Berlin (1842) and ao. Professor at Marburg (1843).

Franz Ferdinand Schwarz worked in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. and PD at the University of Graz, where he studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein, studied at the Center for Hellenic Studies, and became a professor at Graz in 1976.

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Berlin under Franz Bopp, August Boeckh, and Karl Lachmann, and at Oxford. He worked at Rugby School, the British Museum (1844–1848), and as professor of modern languages at Oxford (~1848–1851).

Franz Hessler was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Erlangen-Nuremberg, and Würzburg, where he completed his Ph.D. between 1822 and 1827. In 1852, he became an ordinary member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Franz Josef Meier worked in Indology and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Munich (~1926–1931) and worked as a librarian at the Bavarian State Library from 1937 to 1970.

Franz Joseph Steingass worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing his Ph.D. at Munich (~1842–1846), he taught at Wakefield Grammar School and served as professor and lecturer at the Oriental Institute, Woking (~1884–1903).

Franz Karl Alter worked in linguistics, Indology, and other fields. He studied at Charles University, the University of Vienna, and under Paulinus of St. Bartholomew, later serving as librarian at the Vienna University Library (1779) and working at Vienna (~1779–1804).

Franz Kielhorn was an Indologist who studied at Breslau, Berlin, Leipzig (Ph.D.), Oxford, and Göttingen under Stenzler, Weber, and Benfey. He was professor of Oriental languages at Deccan College (1866–1881) and held the Indology chair at Göttingen from 1881.

Franz Misteli was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Zurich, Bonn, Geneva, and Paris. He became a PD at the University of Bern in 1873, an extra-ordinary professor at Basel in 1874, and Basel's professor of comparative linguistics from 1877 to 1898.

Franz Nikolaus Finck was a linguist who studied at Munich, Paris, and Marburg (Ph.D.). He served as PD at Marburg (1896) and Berlin (1903), taught Oceanian languages at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (~1903–1910), and became ao. Professor in Berlin (1909).

Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary worked in Indology, linguistics, and other fields. He studied at Bonn, Halle-Wittenberg, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, completing his habilitation before serving as PD (1829) and a.o. Professor of theology (1831) at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Franz Specht was a linguist who studied in Berlin and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, August Leskien, Karl Brugmann, and Wilhelm Schulze. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1923–1937), Breslau (1937–1943), Berlin (1943–1945), and Mainz (1946–1949).

Franz Valéry Marie Cumont specialized in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Ghent under Charles Michel, and at Bonn, Berlin, Vienna, and Paris, later serving as teacher (1892) and professor (1906) at Ghent University.

Franz Woepcke worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at Berlin and PD at Bonn, studying under Georg Freytag, Julius Mohl, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux, and taught mathematics at the Französisches Gymnasium Berlin (1856–1858).

Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned degrees at HU Berlin, FU Berlin, Bonn, and Leipzig. He held posts at HU Berlin, Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Oxford, Stadtmuseum Meppen, and was visiting professor at Leipzig (2022–2023).

Franz Xaver Miklosich was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Graz and the University of Vienna. He worked as an amanuensis at the Austrian National Library (1844–1862) and became ao. Professor of Slavic philology at Vienna in 1849.

Franz von Erdmann was a linguist specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at Rostock and Göttingen, he was a PD at Rostock (1818) and served as professor of Oriental languages at Kazan University from approximately 1818 to 1845.
Franz von László was an Indologist. He studied philology at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1941 and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Willibald Kirfel by 1952.
